title: Ada and the Protocol
premise: Ulyana Sandoval, a private security contractor who built her career on being untraceable, receives a calendar invite from Marcus Hale—her handler, dead for eight months—for a meeting the day before a high-stakes diplomatic summit. Following it, she learns Hale faked his death to expose Protocol Vellum, a client-vetting system that launders blacklisted operatives into legitimate security contracts, and that her own scrubbed identity is the linchpin of its cover. Hunted by the firm she serves and shadowed by a rival contractor who may be an ally or a trap, Ulyana must decide whether to trade the one secret worth killing for—her true name and origin—to burn Vellum down before the summit convenes. In the end she testifies under her real name, loses her invisibility forever, but gains a found family among the people who chose to stand with her.
about_author: Ivo Vasquez is a former logistics coordinator for international security firms who turned to fiction after a decade of signing NDAs. He writes thrillers about people whose jobs require them to be forgettable.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Working a routine protection detail in Lisbon, she receives a calendar invite from her dead handler Marcus Hale for tomorrow, 0600, with a location code only he would know. She verifies his death certificate twice. The beat is cold dread: her carefully invisible life has just been addressed by name.

chapters.title: Rules of Disappearance
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, flashback-woven. She reviews her own protocols—burn bags, dead drops, five years of rewritten rules—and decides not to report the anomaly, breaking rule one. Her firm's compliance officer, Dreyer, pings her with an oddly specific check-in. The emotional beat: the first crack in her loyalty.

chapters.title: Six Hundred Hours
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. At the meeting point—an abandoned funicular depot—she finds no Hale, but a burner phone preloaded with files on Protocol Vellum and a voice message cut off mid-sentence by gunfire audio. Someone else arrives; she escapes through the tram tunnels. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Vellum File
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Deciphering the files at a safehouse, she learns Vellum rewrites operatives' identities to place blacklisted contractors inside summit security—and her own file is the template. A tracker ping forces her to move. Beat: the horror of discovering she was never the guard, always the product.

chapters.title: Dreyer's Smile
chapters.summary: Dreyer's POV. The compliance officer reports to firm director Anselm Roth that Ulyana accessed flagged archives, recommending quiet termination. Roth insists on watching her first—she's more useful as bait. Beat: chilling institutional calm; we see how expendable she is.

chapters.title: Kestrel
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ambushed in a parking structure by rival contractor Kestrel, she fights free, but Kestrel lets her go deliberately, whispering 'Hale owed me.' Uncertain if Kestrel is hunter or defector, Ulyana takes a risk and arranges contact. Beat: wary attraction to trust.

chapters.title: What Hale Owed
chapters.summary: Alternating Ulyana/Kestrel POV. On a cargo ferry, Kestrel reveals Hale recruited him to verify the Vellum files before going public; Hale's death was staged—or botched. He gives Ulyana half a decryption key Hale split between them. Beat: two loners negotiating the terms of alliance.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Using the partial key, she finds a hidden layer: video of Hale alive, recorded three weeks ago, naming Roth as Vellum's architect and warning that the summit's host government is complicit. Then Dreyer calls—offering her a promotion. Beat: temptation versus truth.

chapters.title: The Promotion
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She takes the meeting, playing loyal while mapping the firm's summit deployment from Dreyer's own briefing materials. Roth appears briefly and compliments her discretion; she recognizes the man from her buried past. Beat: performing loyalty while it dies inside her.

chapters.title: Origin Story
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, deep flashback. Her real name, her recruitment out of a witness-protection aftermath, and how Hale forged the identity that saved her—the same forgery technique Vellum industrialized. Beat: grief and fury braided together; the secret has a face now.

chapters.title: Split Key
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel admits he's been feeding location data to a third party to protect his sister, whom Vellum holds as leverage. Ulyana must decide whether betrayal under duress is forgivable. Beat: loyalty tested against compassion.

chapters.title: Safehouse Burning
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The firm hits their safehouse using Kestrel's leaked coordinates; they escape separated, and Ulyana is wounded. A teenage hacker, Priya, whom Hale had also contacted, pulls them out via transit cameras. Beat: the found family begins assembling itself around Hale's plan.

chapters.title: Priya's Ledger
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. From a squat above a laundromat, Priya shows them Vellum's live roster—dozens of rewritten operatives embedded in summit security, any of whom could be triggered. The full key will need both halves plus a passphrase only Hale knew. Beat: hope with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: The Dead Man's Schedule
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Tracing Hale's patterns, she deduces where he'd hide—and finds evidence he's been moving between cities using Vellum's own identity-rewrite pipeline. Either he's alive, or someone is wearing his ghost. Beat: vertigo; nothing about identity can be trusted, including grief.

chapters.title: Roth's Offer
chapters.summary: Roth's POV. Roth summons Ulyana privately, revealing he knows her original name and offers to restore it—clean record, new life—if she delivers Kestrel and the key. He frames it as mercy. Beat: the devil offering her back her self.

chapters.title: Confession at the Laundromat
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She tells Kestrel and Priya everything, including Roth's offer, surrendering the secret she's guarded all book. Instead of judgment, they plan around it. Beat: the theme lands—truth offered freely binds tighter than loyalty extracted.

chapters.title: Counter-Protocol
chapters.summary: Full team POV rotation. They build the play: use Roth's offer to get Ulyana inside the summit perimeter, let Priya ride the firm's network, have Kestrel draw Dreyer off. Each accepts their role knowing some version of this fails. Beat: grim, tender commitment.

chapters.title: Summit Eve
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Inside the perimeter, she meets the man wearing Hale's identity—a Vellum operative implanted with Hale's forged legend, including memories of her. Confronting him cracks her certainty about what's real. Beat: identity as weapon turned inward.

chapters.title: The Real Hale
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Revealed: Hale has been captive in Roth's custody, his identity harvested; he escaped during summit setup and reaches Ulyana through the old location code. Reunion is brief and unsentimental—he hands over the passphrase and tells her to finish it without him. Beat: mentor passing the burden on.

chapters.title: Trigger Night
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, rapid cuts. The summit opens; Roth activates the embedded operatives; Priya races the kill-switch through the network; Kestrel trades himself to buy time; Ulyana fights to the broadcast hub. Beat: controlled chaos, every debt called in at once.

chapters.title: Her Real Name
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. With Priya's access and Hale's passphrase, she broadcasts the Vellum ledger to every delegate's terminal—and introduces herself by her true name, on record, unredacted. Roth is arrested by the very delegates he owned; Dreyer vanishes into the machine he served. Beat: catharsis through exposure.

chapters.title: After the Summit
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, epilogue tone. Weeks later: Hale recovering, Kestrel released after his sister's rescue, Priya arguing about apartment leases none of them can legally sign. Ulyana, unemployable and finally visible, realizes the family assembled around Hale's plan is the first thing she hasn't had to forge. Beat: quiet, earned belonging.
